name: Keep rhythm with a metronome
blurb: The unglamorous skill underneath every other musical skill. Playing genuinely in time — not approximately in time — is trainable and immediately audible.
gear: Any instrument, or just your hands
steps: Clap quarter notes with the click at 80 bpm until the click disappears underneath your clap. That disappearance is the target sensation.
Subdivide: clap eighths, then triplets, then sixteenths, against the same click.
Move the click to beats 2 and 4 only, which is much harder and far more musical.
Practise at slow tempos — 50 bpm exposes every timing flaw that 120 hides.
Play a piece you know at 60% speed with the click, then raise it in 5 bpm steps, dropping back whenever it gets sloppy.
Record yourself against a click and listen back for drift.
tips: If you can still hear the click clearly on every beat, you are slightly off it.
Rushing is far more common than dragging, especially in loud or fast passages.
proof: You play a full piece with the click on 2 and 4 without drifting, and it sounds locked on playback.
